title: Stories and what happens in them
description: Tell what happened, from the first line to the end.

explanation.summary: B1 ends where a story begins: somebody tells what happened. The preterite carries it, and a small set of nouns names the parts of every story ever told.

sections.heading: The parts of a story
sections.body: El relato is the story itself, and la trama is what happens in it. El personaje is who it happens to. El nudo is where everything tangles, and el desenlace is where it comes undone.

examples.es: El relato empieza en un pueblo pequeño.
examples.en: The story starts in a small town.

examples.es: La trama me tuvo despierto toda la noche.
examples.en: The plot kept me awake all night.

sections.heading: Who tells it
sections.body: El narrador is the voice that tells the story. El héroe wins and el villano loses, and la moraleja is what the story was trying to say. Contar is the verb for the whole act: cuento, cuentas, cuenta.

examples.es: El narrador cuenta lo que vio.
examples.en: The narrator tells what he saw.

examples.es: La moraleja es no rendirse nunca.
examples.en: The moral is never to give up.

exercises.prompt: Pair each word with its translation.
exercises.note: A story is told in the preterite: empezó, pasó, terminó.
